prompt:
UI design mockup of a screen of an AI software factory console, in its existing "Mission control" design: thin-bordered instrument panels with small corner marks, cyan as the system colour, amber as the one signal that needs a human, monospace for refs, times and figures, a system sans for text, sizes 11 to 18 px, weights 400 and 600 only, everything exact and calm.

Dark theme: page #070b12, panels and columns #0b111a, raised panels #0f1723, cards #111b28, hairlines #1a2636, panel borders #263649, text #dfe7f1, muted grey #93a1b5, faint grey #7c8ba0, cyan #4fcbe2, amber #f4b13e filling buttons with dark text, amber text #f6bd5a, done green #5cc98f, failed red muted #c98a8a.

A desktop browser window 1280 px wide and 800 px high, drawn at high resolution so the 13 px card text is crisp and legible. Flat, no browser chrome, no device frame, the screen fills the whole image.

The shell is fixed and must look like this. A quiet top bar: "Factory console", the project select "ai-software-factory-code ▾", a bordered "NEW TASK", the words "COSTS", "METRICS", "RESOURCES", "SETTINGS", "POLICY", "NOTIFICATIONS" in small capitals, a small moon and sun toggle, "sebastian", "Log out". Under it one thin status strip of cells split by hairlines: "● waiting on you | 2 working | 2 need you | €61.40 / €120.00 ▬▬▬▭▭ 51 % | ↻ bump in 20 min | GitHub: 1 open pull request", with "2 need you" in amber. Then the main area. The chat panel on the left, 40 percent of the width, a raised panel with a thin cyan rule on its top edge, its header "Chat  project agent · ai-software-factory-code" and "New", its log holding two short turns, "sebastian: What waits on me?" and "project agent: Two cards. Plan one face needs its promises settled, and #2101 needs two lines changed by a human.", and its composer at the foot, "Ask or tell the project…" with a cyan "Send". The board on the right, 60 percent: a header row "BOARD", a small mono find box "Find: a word, #612, plan:558", "Documents", "↻ routines ▾", "?". Then four columns side by side, heads in small capitals with a count: "NEEDS YOU 2" (the widest column, about 245 px, its own amber tint fill, an amber rule and amber corner marks), "QUEUED 3 ▾" (about 160 px), "IN PROGRESS 1 ▾" (about 200 px), "DONE 3 ▾" (the narrowest, about 135 px). Cards sit on the columns with 1 px hairline borders and 8 px padding.

The drawer is open: docked at the right edge of the main area, about 590 px wide, over the board, from the top of the main area to the foot. The chat stays in view at the left. The strip of board between the chat and the drawer is dimmed. The drawer is a raised panel with a hairline left border and holds the opened card.

The opened card #1850, words spelled exactly.
Tabs: "Overview" (selected), "Chat", "Activity", "Files", and a close "×".
Head: the ref "#1850" and the state "needs you 3 h" with an amber dot. Title: Plan "one face" finished, but no test checked its 5 promises. Settle each one. Why line: Until all 5 are settled, the plan stays open and holds production deploys. Place: plan one face, 5 cards, all ended.
The ask block: "Promise 1 of 5" with ‹ and › arrows. The promise: Every card that asks shows one decision block. Under it: The work is on main. No test checked it. The two answers, each with its effect line:
"Run the tests now", suggested by the project agent. Effect: Runs the plan's tests on main and records each result.
"Drop this promise". Effect: Takes the promise off the plan.
"Drop this promise" is the pressed answer, so its note field shows: an empty text box with the hint "Say why this promise can go." Then one "Send" button for the block.
The summary, one short paragraph: The last card, #2011, closed without a merge. Its work was already on main through another card, so the factory never ran the plan's tests. When all 5 promises are settled, the plan closes and production deploys go on.
Five closed folds, in this order, each one row with ▸ and a hint at the right in the muted grey: "The full brief" (hint "5 promises and the evidence"), "The plan" (hint "one face · 5 cards · 4 merged, 1 closed"), "The card's life" (hint "3 h waiting · no session"), "What each session got" (hint "no session yet"), "Other actions" (hint "End the card, and 1 more").

Direction D, "the labelled rows", for the opened card:
The opened card is a list of labelled rows. A tab row at the top with "Overview" underlined in cyan. Then a two-column grid: a narrow left column of labels in faint small capitals, right-aligned, and the content in the wide right column, hairlines between the rows. "ASK" with the title at 18 px semibold. "WHY" with the why line at 14 px. "WHERE" with "plan one face · 5 cards, all ended · ● needs you 3 h · #1850" in mono 12 px. Then the ask block spanning the right column, with a 3 px amber bar and an amber band "Promise 1 of 5 ‹ ›", the promise and the line under it. "ANSWERS" with the answers as a list, each a radio with its label in semibold and the effect line after it: "Run the tests now" first with "suggested by the project agent" in faint grey, then "Drop this promise", pressed, with its note field under it. One amber "Send" under the list. "SUMMARY" with the summary paragraph. Then the five folds as rows, each fold's name in the left column in small capitals with ▸ and its hint in the right column. On the phone each label sits above its content.

Legible UI text with exact spelling. Every word above appears once, where it is placed. Nothing invented, no lorem ipsum, no extra cards, buttons or labels. Normal states whisper, exceptional states speak: the Needs you cards and their amber answer buttons are the loudest things on the screen, queued and in progress cards are quiet, done cards are the quietest. Made by a top product design studio. Not a template, not a generic admin dashboard.
